newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar adopts measures to protect new bourse.
newsitem.headline: Qatar adopts measures to protect new bourse.

text.p: The Doha Securities Market (DSM) said on Monday it has adopted tough measures to curb volatile and speculative trading in the seven-day-old bourse.
"Computers have been programmed in such a way that they will not register the price of shares that rise beyond 10 percent," Ghanem al-Hammadi, DSM director, told reporters.
"Supervisors in the dealing room have also been instructed to keep a watch on price fluctuations," he added.
Bullish investors have pushed up the price of key shares since the DSM officially opened its floor to local investors on May 27.
"There have been reports of a sudden increase in share prices followed by an abrupt plunge at various stock markets because of rumours. We do not want such shocks to happen at DSM," Hammadi said.
At present, only Qatari nationals are allowed to trade in stocks from Sunday through Thursday from 9.00 to 10.30 a.m.
But proposals are being considered to open the bourse to Gulf Arab nationals and to foreigners in future.
"We want to minimise rumours and shocks and encourage stability and transparency in the stock market," said Hammadi.
"The system of checks and balances introduced at the DSM will ensure just that".
Khalid al-Amoudi, head of the DSM surveillance department, said auditors would also keep a watch on trade by dealers and brokers to ensure a fair deal for investors.
Shares of 17 local companies, capitalised at $1.9 billion, are currently traded at DSM.

But officials hope the number of listed firms and the capitalisation will rise sharply after the government offloads some of its shares in wholly state-owned companies for public subscription as part of a privatisation programme.
DSM is also authorised to handle the trade in government bonds and treasury bills.
Officials hope the bourse will encourage citizens to plough their money back into the wealthy Gulf Arab oil state rather than invest in the West's developed financial markets.
